## Literature

- Cornwell & Ackerly 2009
- Ogle 2014 - wood density
- Fischer et al 2025 (in review) - Global Wood Density Database. partition variance at different levels of biological organisation and with and quantify correlations with climate variables. They fit exactly the same structure for the mixed effect model that I ended up using, including the two climate variables, the average species value and the centered deviation from the average. Reassuring that they converged on the same approach. They cite an Gelman reference (guru statistician) where they recommend this approach for LMMs when "Predictors and Group Effects Correlate"  https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.1010095

# Data preparation

```{r}
# See overall amount of taxa in dataset
data_traits_climate_raw |>
  pull(taxon_name) |>
  unique() |> 
  length()
```

```{r}
# δ13C transformation follows Cernusak & Ubierna:
# Carbon Isotope Effects in Relation to CO2 Assimilation by Tree Canopies
# https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-92698-4_9

data_traits_climate <-  data_traits_climate_raw |>
  # Drop photosynthetic_pathway rows (categorical, not a modelled trait)
  filter(trait_name %in% c("huber_value","leaf_N_per_area","leaf_area","leaf_delta13C","leaf_mass_per_area","wood_density","seed_dry_mass")) |>
  # Extract collection year from date strings; average if a range is given
  # NOTE: year / delta13c_a are computed for all rows but only used for leaf_delta13C
  mutate(year = map_dbl(collection_date, function(d) {
    years <- as.numeric(unlist(regmatches(d, gregexpr("\\d{4}", d))))
    if (length(years) > 1) round(mean(years)) else years[1]
  })) |>
  # Estimate atmospheric δ13C at time of collection using a linear time trend
  mutate(delta13c_a = 39.7336 - 0.0239*year) |>
  # Step 1: convert raw leaf δ13C (‰) to isotope discrimination Δ (‰)
  #   Δ = (δ_atm - δ_leaf) / (1 + δ_leaf/1000)
  mutate(value = ifelse(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C",(delta13c_a- value) / (1+(value/1000)), value)) |>
  # Step 2: convert Δ to ci/ca ratio (proxy for intrinsic WUE)
  #   ci/ca = (Δ - a) / (b - a)  where a = 4.4‰ (diffusion), b = 27‰ (carboxylation)
  #   Higher ci/ca → lower WUE
  # Also, just convert huber value to more readable units (mm2/cm2)
  mutate(value = ifelse(trait_name == "huber_value",value*1e2, value)) |>
  mutate(value = ifelse(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C",(value - 4.4)/(27-4.4), value)) |>
  # remove trait, climate, woody rows with NA data
  drop_na(value, annual_precipitation, average_temperature, woody) |>
  # NOTE: range-based select relies on column ordering from the parquet file;
  # 'cell' must fall between decimal_longitude and life_stage for ncell to work below
  select(decimal_longitude:life_stage, woody) |>
  # log transform precipitation
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation = log(annual_precipitation),
    # leaf_delta13C is already on a bounded (0-1) ci/ca scale; log-transform all other traits
    log_value = ifelse(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C", value, log(value))
  ) |>
  # Count how many unique climate cells each species appears per trait
  group_by(taxon_name, trait_name) |>
  mutate(ncell = length(unique((cell)))) |> 
  ungroup() |>
  # Require species to appear in at least 2 climate cells (needed to estimate intraspecific variation)
    filter(ncell > 1) |>
  # huber_value and wood_density are only meaningful for woody species
  filter(!(trait_name %in% c("wood_density", "huber_value") & woody != "woody"))
```

# Mean taxon-trait value per cell

```{r}
data_traits_climate <- data_traits_climate %>%
  group_by(annual_precipitation,
         average_temperature,
         cell,
        #  dataset_id,
         taxon_name,
         trait_name,
         woody,
         log_annual_precipitation
         ) %>%
  summarise(log_value = mean(log_value),
  value = mean(value),
  decimal_longitude = decimal_longitude[1],
  decimal_latitude = decimal_latitude[1])
```

# Data preparation - climate centroids and deviation

```{r}
# --- Compute global scaling parameters for climate variables ---
# distinct(cell) ensures each climate cell is weighted equally regardless of how
# many species observations it has (otherwise high-diversity cells would dominate).
# These scalers are applied to all traits combined (union of all cells, not per-trait).
log_annual_precipitation_scaler <- data_traits_climate %>%
  distinct(cell,.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pull(log_annual_precipitation) %>%
  scale()

log_annual_precipitation_scaler_center <- attr(log_annual_precipitation_scaler, "scaled:center")

log_annual_precipitation_scaler_scale <- attr(log_annual_precipitation_scaler, "scaled:scale")

average_temperature_scaler <- data_traits_climate %>%
  distinct(cell,.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pull(average_temperature)%>%
  scale()

average_temperature_scaler_center <- attr(average_temperature_scaler, "scaled:center")

average_temperature_scaler_scale <- attr(average_temperature_scaler, "scaled:scale")

data_traits_climate |>
  # --- Step C: Standardise climate variables (z-score, cell-weighted) ---
  mutate(std_log_annual_precipitation = (log_annual_precipitation - log_annual_precipitation_scaler_center)/log_annual_precipitation_scaler_scale,
         std_average_temperature = (average_temperature - average_temperature_scaler_center)/average_temperature_scaler_scale) |>
  # --- Step D: Extract one climate value per (species × cell) combination ---
  # Nest so that each row represents one unique cell a species occupies.
  # [1] is safe here because log_annual_precipitation / average_temperature are
  # raster-derived and identical for all observations within the same cell.
  group_by(taxon_name, cell) |>
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$log_annual_precipitation[1]),
    average_temperature_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$average_temperature[1]),
    std_log_annual_precipitation_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$std_log_annual_precipitation[1]),
    std_average_temperature_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$std_average_temperature[1])
  ) |>
  # --- Step E: Compute each species' mean climate position ---
  # The mean is taken over all cells the species occupies across ALL traits jointly.
  # A species' mean climate position is therefore the same for all its traits.
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_mn = mean(log_annual_precipitation_cell),
    average_temperature_mn = mean(average_temperature_cell)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    std_log_annual_precipitation_mn = mean(std_log_annual_precipitation_cell),
    std_average_temperature_mn = mean(std_average_temperature_cell)
  ) |>
  # --- Step F: Restore individual observations and compute intraspecific deviations ---
  # Each observation's climate position minus its species' mean climate position.
  # This within-species deviation is the intraspecific (plasticity) component used in models.
  unnest(data) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(log_annual_precipitation_c = log_annual_precipitation - log_annual_precipitation_mn,
    average_temperature_c = average_temperature - average_temperature_mn,
    std_log_annual_precipitation_c = std_log_annual_precipitation - std_log_annual_precipitation_mn,
    std_average_temperature_c = std_average_temperature - std_average_temperature_mn) -> data_traits_climate
```  

# Climate variable check: BIO5 & BIO10 vs average temperature

BIO5 (max temperature of the warmest month) and BIO10 (mean temperature of the
warmest quarter) are extracted at the same coordinates as the trait data and
correlated against `average_temperature` (BIO1, annual mean temperature) to check
how well the annual mean represents warm-season temperature across the dataset.

```{r}
# Australia tif just used to crop extent
australia <- terra::rast("data/australia.tif")

bio5_bio10_rasters <-
  file.path("data/wc2.1_30s_bio", c("wc2.1_30s_bio_5.tif", "wc2.1_30s_bio_10.tif","wc2.1_30s_bio_12.tif")) |>
  terra::rast() |>
  terra::crop(australia)

# One extraction per unique location actually present in the trait data (not per
# observation), then join back on to avoid redundant raster lookups
trait_coords <- data_traits_climate |>
  distinct(decimal_longitude, decimal_latitude, average_temperature)

trait_coords_vect <- terra::vect(
  trait_coords,
  geom = c("decimal_longitude", "decimal_latitude"),
  crs = terra::crs(bio5_bio10_rasters)
)

bio5_bio10_values <-
  terra::extract(bio5_bio10_rasters, trait_coords_vect, ID = FALSE) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(bio5_max_temp_warmest_month = wc2.1_30s_bio_5,
         bio10_mean_temp_warmest_quarter = wc2.1_30s_bio_10,
         bio12_mean_annual_precipitation = wc2.1_30s_bio_12) |>
  bind_cols(trait_coords)
```

```{r}
cor.test(bio5_bio10_values$average_temperature, bio5_bio10_values$bio5_max_temp_warmest_month)
cor.test(bio5_bio10_values$average_temperature, bio5_bio10_values$bio10_mean_temp_warmest_quarter)
```

```{r}
# Background: climate at the centre of every land cell of the Australia mask
# (0.05 deg, ~278k cells), i.e. the full Australian climate space, not just trait locations
bio1_bio5_bio10_rasters <-
  file.path("data/wc2.1_30s_bio", c("wc2.1_30s_bio_1.tif", "wc2.1_30s_bio_5.tif", "wc2.1_30s_bio_10.tif","wc2.1_30s_bio_12.tif")) |>
  terra::rast() |>
  terra::crop(australia)

australia_climate <-
  terra::extract(
    bio1_bio5_bio10_rasters,
    terra::as.data.frame(australia, xy = TRUE)[, c("x", "y")],
    ID = FALSE
  ) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(average_temperature = wc2.1_30s_bio_1,
         bio5_max_temp_warmest_month = wc2.1_30s_bio_5,
         bio10_mean_temp_warmest_quarter = wc2.1_30s_bio_10,
         bio12_mean_annual_precipitation = wc2.1_30s_bio_12) |>
  drop_na()

bind_rows(
  australia_climate |> mutate(source = "All of Australia"),
  bio5_bio10_values |> mutate(source = "Trait locations")
) |>
  select(source, average_temperature, bio5_max_temp_warmest_month, bio10_mean_temp_warmest_quarter,bio12_mean_annual_precipitation) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(bio5_max_temp_warmest_month, bio10_mean_temp_warmest_quarter,bio12_mean_annual_precipitation),
    names_to = "bio_var", values_to = "bio_value"
  ) |>
  mutate(bio_var = recode(bio_var,
    bio5_max_temp_warmest_month     = "BIO05: max temp of warmest month",
    bio10_mean_temp_warmest_quarter = "BIO10: mean temp of warmest quarter",
    bio12_mean_annual_precipitation = "BIO12: mean annual precipitation"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(average_temperature, bio_value, colour = source)) +
  # Background (all of Australia) first so trait locations sit on top
  geom_hex(data = \(d) filter(d, source == "All of Australia"), size = 0.3, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, source == "Trait locations"), alpha = 0.3) +
  # Smooths use fixed colours: the all-of-Australia line is darker than its points so it stays visible
  geom_smooth(data = \(d) filter(d, source == "All of Australia"), method = "lm", colour = "grey20", fill = "grey20") +
  geom_smooth(data = \(d) filter(d, source == "Trait locations"), method = "lm", colour = "#0072B2", fill = "#0072B2") +
  facet_wrap(~bio_var, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("All of Australia" = "grey60", "Trait locations" = "#0072B2"), name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1)),
  fill = "none") +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = expression(paste("Average temperature, BIO1 (", degree * C, ")")), y = "") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12), axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
        legend.position = "bottom") -> cor_plots


ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = bio1_bio5_bio10_rasters[[1]]) +
  labs(title = expression(paste("Average temperature, BIO1 (", degree * C,")"))) -> temp_plot

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = bio1_bio5_bio10_rasters[[4]]) +
  labs(title = expression(paste("Mean annual precipitation, BIO12 (mm)"))) +
  scale_fill_continuous(trans = "log") -> prec_plot

cor_plots/(temp_plot|prec_plot)
ggsave("outputs/figures/FigureS1.png", height = 8, width = 10)
```

# Data summaries

```{r}
# Taxa with multiple cells
data_traits_climate |>
  pull(taxon_name) |>
  unique() |>
  length()

# Taxa per trait with multiple cells
data_traits_climate |>
  group_by(trait_name) |>
  summarise(n_taxon = length(unique(taxon_name)))

# Trait range table: 0.1% and 99.9% quantiles of the cell-mean trait values (robust to a
# few implausible extreme records) and the fold variation between them. Built from
# data_traits_climate, which holds exactly the modelled rows (the grey dots in Figure 3).
# Units as transformed above (huber_value in mm2/cm2, leaf_delta13C as ci/ca).
source("R/export_trait_range_table.R")
trait_range_table <- build_trait_range_table(data_traits_climate)
trait_range_table

export_trait_range_table(trait_range_table, "outputs/tables/TableS1.docx")

data_traits_climate |> 
  group_by(trait_name) |>
  nest() %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  slice(3) %>%
  unnest(data) %>%
  group_by(taxon_name) %>%
  summarise(value = median(value)) %>%
  pull(value) %>%
  hist()

# Minimum and maximum of climate values
data_traits_climate |>
  ungroup() |>
  summarise(min_prec = min(annual_precipitation, na.rm = T),
  max_prec = max(annual_precipitation, na.rm = T),
  min_temp = min(average_temperature, na.rm = T),
  max_temp = max(average_temperature, na.rm = T))
```

# Random-effect structure comparison - woody

Before fitting the functional group comparison models: compare random-intercept and random-slope variances
pooled across growth forms against estimated separately for woody and non-woody taxa
(fixed effects identical), by AIC from glmmTMB.

```{r}
source("R/compare_random_effect_structures.R")
woody_split_traits <- setdiff(unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name), WOODY_ONLY_TRAITS)

re_aic <- compare_re_aic(data_traits_climate, woody_split_traits)
re_aic |> arrange(trait, env, dAIC)

export_re_aic_table(re_aic, "outputs/tables/TableS6.docx")
```

# Plot combined distribution of responses, MAP

```{r}
source("R/fit_model2d_frequentist_4panel.R")

traits <- unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name)

Figure_3_panels <- list()

for (trait in traits) {
  cat(trait, ":  ")
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)
  fit_model2d_frequentist_4panel_out_prec <- fit_model2d_frequentist_4panel(data_model, ind_variable = "log_annual_precipitation")
  Figure_3_panels[[trait]] <- fit_model2d_frequentist_4panel_out_prec[[2]]
}

# Third column of each trait's row: density of per-species within-species (intraspecific)
# slopes, titled with its trait label (set in fit_model2d_frequentist_4panel()); give
# every panel the same x-axis title.
Figure_3_hist_panels <- imap(Figure_3_panels, ~ {
  .x[[3]] +
    labs(x = "Within-species response to MAP") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
})

patchwork::wrap_plots(list(Figure_3_hist_panels[[2]],
Figure_3_hist_panels[[4]],
Figure_3_hist_panels[[3]],
Figure_3_hist_panels[[1]],
Figure_3_hist_panels[[5]],
Figure_3_hist_panels[[7]],
Figure_3_hist_panels[[6]]), ncol = 3, tag = "new") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")

ggsave("outputs/figures/FigureS2.png", height = 8, width = 13.33)
```

# Figure 2
```{r}
# Figure 2: within-species share of climate-associated trait
# variation, S_w = k r / (k r + 1), with r = (B_w / B_m)^2 per posterior draw and k at its
# observed value, var(Env_w) / var(Env_m). S_w draws are cached per trait in
# outputs/model_fits/within_share/ (rebuilt automatically when a fit is newer).
source("R/within_share.R")

traits <- c("leaf_delta13C","leaf_area","leaf_mass_per_area","seed_dry_mass","leaf_N_per_area","huber_value","wood_density")

# Forest plots of S_w on a shared logit axis (most values lie close to 0), at the
# observed k (floor)and k = 1 (ceiling)
figure2 <- plot_within_share_forest(traits)
ggsave("outputs/figures/Figure2.png", figure2, height = 6, width = 9)

figureS4 <- plot_within_share_forest(traits, k = 1)
ggsave("outputs/figures/FigureS4.png", figureS4, height = 6, width = 9)

# S_w as k rises from the observed value to 1 (dense grid of 100 k values), with
# 8 evenly spaced k values from observed to 1 marked as points
within_share_curve <- plot_within_share_curve(traits, n_k = 100, k_mid = 0.5, n_points = 8)
ggsave("outputs/figures/FigureS5.png", within_share_curve, height = 14, width = 9)

# Supplementary tables for the S_w figures: observed k (with k and the Env_m-Env_w
# orthogonality check) and k = 1
export_within_share_table(traits, k = "observed", "outputs/tables/TableS2.docx")
export_within_share_table(traits, k = 1, "outputs/tables/TableS7.docx")
```

```{r}
# Combined-case metric: (intra slope / inter slope)^2 * (var(deviation from centroid) / var(centroids))
# Using the all-species model only (combined case), summarised by the posterior median slopes.
combined_trait_metric <- map_dfr(unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name), function(trait) {
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)

  fits <- readRDS(paste0("outputs/model_fits/fit2d_bayesian/", trait, ".RDS"))

  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      env = "MAP",
      inter_slope = median(posterior::as_draws_df(fits[[1]])[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_mn"]]),
      intra_slope = median(posterior::as_draws_df(fits[[1]])[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_c"]]),
      var_centroids = var(data_model$std_log_annual_precipitation_mn, na.rm = TRUE),
      var_deviations = var(data_model$std_log_annual_precipitation_c, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
      mutate(metric = (intra_slope / inter_slope)^2 * (var_deviations / var_centroids)),

    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      env = "MAT",
      inter_slope = median(posterior::as_draws_df(fits[[2]])[["b_std_average_temperature_mn"]]),
      intra_slope = median(posterior::as_draws_df(fits[[2]])[["b_std_average_temperature_c"]]),
      var_centroids = var(data_model$std_average_temperature_mn, na.rm = TRUE),
      var_deviations = var(data_model$std_average_temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
      mutate(metric = (intra_slope / inter_slope)^2 * (var_deviations / var_centroids))
  )
}) |>
  arrange(env, trait)
```

```{r}
# Woody/non-woody split metric: (intra slope / inter slope)^2 * (var(deviation from centroid) / var(centroids))
# Uses the group-specific posterior slopes from the woody interaction model. The all-species metric above is the combined-case analogue.
woody_split_traits <- setdiff(unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name), c("huber_value", "wood_density"))

woody_split_trait_metric <- map_dfr(woody_split_traits, function(trait) {
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)

  fits <- readRDS(paste0("outputs/model_fits/fit2d_bayesian_woody/", trait, ".RDS"))

  draw_map <- posterior::as_draws_df(fits[[1]]) |> as_tibble()
  draw_mat <- posterior::as_draws_df(fits[[2]]) |> as_tibble()

  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      group = "non-woody",
      env = "MAP",
      inter_slope = median(draw_map[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_mn"]]),
      intra_slope = median(draw_map[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_c"]]),
      var_centroids = var((data_model |> filter(woody == "non-woody"))$std_log_annual_precipitation_mn, na.rm = TRUE),
      var_deviations = var((data_model |> filter(woody == "non-woody"))$std_log_annual_precipitation_c, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
      mutate(metric = (intra_slope / inter_slope)^2 * (var_deviations / var_centroids)),

    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      group = "woody",
      env = "MAP",
      inter_slope = median(draw_map[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_mn"]] + draw_map[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_mn:woodywoody"]]),
      intra_slope = median(draw_map[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_c"]] + draw_map[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_c:woodywoody"]]),
      var_centroids = var((data_model |> filter(woody == "woody"))$std_log_annual_precipitation_mn, na.rm = TRUE),
      var_deviations = var((data_model |> filter(woody == "woody"))$std_log_annual_precipitation_c, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
      mutate(metric = (intra_slope / inter_slope)^2 * (var_deviations / var_centroids)),

    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      group = "non-woody",
      env = "MAT",
      inter_slope = median(draw_mat[["b_std_average_temperature_mn"]]),
      intra_slope = median(draw_mat[["b_std_average_temperature_c"]]),
      var_centroids = var((data_model |> filter(woody == "non-woody"))$std_average_temperature_mn, na.rm = TRUE),
      var_deviations = var((data_model |> filter(woody == "non-woody"))$std_average_temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
      mutate(metric = (intra_slope / inter_slope)^2 * (var_deviations / var_centroids)),

    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      group = "woody",
      env = "MAT",
      inter_slope = median(draw_mat[["b_std_average_temperature_mn"]] + draw_mat[["b_std_average_temperature_mn:woodywoody"]]),
      intra_slope = median(draw_mat[["b_std_average_temperature_c"]] + draw_mat[["b_std_average_temperature_c:woodywoody"]]),
      var_centroids = var((data_model |> filter(woody == "woody"))$std_average_temperature_mn, na.rm = TRUE),
      var_deviations = var((data_model |> filter(woody == "woody"))$std_average_temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
      mutate(metric = (intra_slope / inter_slope)^2 * (var_deviations / var_centroids))
  )
}) |>
  arrange(env, trait, group)

woody_split_trait_metric %>% 
select(-inter_slope, -intra_slope)
```

```{r}
# Figure 5-like plot of the metric components:
# posterior distributions for inter- and intraspecific slopes, with the variance
# component shown as a point estimate rather than a posterior distribution.
trait_order <- c(
  "leaf_N_per_area",
  "leaf_delta13C",
  "leaf_mass_per_area",
  "seed_dry_mass",
  "leaf_area",
  "wood_density",
  "huber_value"
)

combined_metric_slope_draws <- map_dfr(unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name), function(trait) {
  fits <- readRDS(paste0("outputs/model_fits/fit2d_bayesian/", trait, ".RDS"))

  draw_map <- posterior::as_draws_df(fits[[1]]) |> as_tibble()
  draw_mat <- posterior::as_draws_df(fits[[2]]) |> as_tibble()

  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      env = "MAP",
      term = "inter",
      value = draw_map[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_mn"]]
    ),
    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      env = "MAP",
      term = "intra",
      value = draw_map[["b_std_log_annual_precipitation_c"]]
    ),
    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      env = "MAT",
      term = "inter",
      value = draw_mat[["b_std_average_temperature_mn"]]
    ),
    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      env = "MAT",
      term = "intra",
      value = draw_mat[["b_std_average_temperature_c"]]
    )
  )
}) |>
  mutate(trait = factor(trait, levels = trait_order))

combined_metric_var_est <- map_dfr(unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name), function(trait) {
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)

  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      env = "MAP",
      term = "variance",
      value = var(data_model$std_log_annual_precipitation_c, na.rm = TRUE) /
        var(data_model$std_log_annual_precipitation_mn, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    tibble(
      trait = trait,
      env = "MAT",
      term = "variance",
      value = var(data_model$std_average_temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE) /
        var(data_model$std_average_temperature_mn, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )
}) |>
  mutate(trait = factor(trait, levels = trait_order))

combined_metric_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_violin(
    data = combined_metric_slope_draws,
    aes(x = trait, y = value, fill = term),
    trim = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.7,
    width = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = combined_metric_var_est,
    aes(x = trait, y = value, colour = term),
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_grid(term ~ env, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10.5),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(y = "Value") +
  xlab("Trait") +
  scale_fill_okabeito(order = c(1, 2), breaks = c("inter", "intra")) +
  scale_colour_okabeito(order = c(3), breaks = c("variance"))

combined_metric_plot
```
